title: Long-form writing with cross-page consistency checking
goal: Prove lab.common.longform.write_long_document (EXP-052's ask-derived section titling, wired onto the existing deterministic outline/rewriter/document-writer pieces) produces a real multi-page document, and that lab.common.working_memory's cross-page consistency check (EXP-053) both stays silent on a genuinely consistent document and fires on a deliberately injected contradiction, naming the specific conflicting pages and values.
method: Two 6-7 leaf documents from the same ask: one internally consistent, one identical except a later page restates an earlier page's fact about the same person with a different value. Both run through lab.common.longform.write_long_document end to end, checked for coverage, citation integrity, and the consistency flags lab.common.working_memory actually produced.

metrics.document_sample:
Ravi Sharma lives at 14 MG Road, Pune 411001. [C0] Ravi Sharma works at ABC Pvt Ltd. [C1] Ravi Sharma signed on 5 January 2024. [C2] Ravi Sharma reports to Deepak Verma. [C3]

Meera Iyer
Meera Iyer lives at 22 Lake View Road, Chennai 600028. [C4]
Meera Iyer works at Zenith Corp. [C5]

Priya Nair
Priya Nair lives at 9 Residency Road, Bengaluru 560001. [C6]
Priya Nair works at Globex Inc. [C7]

results_prose: Clean 6-leaf document: 0 consistency flag(s) (expect 0), coverage 1.0, 0 broken citation(s). Conflicting 7-leaf document (identical, plus a later page restating Ravi Sharma's address with a different value): 1 flag(s) -- the address conflict was caught: [{'leaf_id': 'E0001', 'subject': 'Ravi Sharma', 'verb_lemma': 'live', 'new_object': '88 New Colony Road , Nagpur 440001', 'conflicts_with_leaf_id': 'E0000', 'prior_object': '14 MG Road , Pune 411001'}].
conclusion: Both mechanisms work as intended: a genuinely consistent multi-page document produces zero false-positive flags, and a deliberately injected later-page contradiction about the same person and the same fact (address) is caught, naming exactly which earlier page it conflicts with and what the two values were -- not just 'something is wrong somewhere'. This closes EXP-053's gap directly: a check that previously did not exist at all for long-form writing, built on lab.common.working_memory's bounded 'RAM' (subject-verb-object triples only, never full page text kept once a page is behind it).
scale_down: 6-7 leaves, one deliberately injected conflict -- a proof the mechanism works and stays quiet when it should, not a scale test (EXP-077 already measured generative fidelity at 80 leaves; this is a different mechanism, checked separately).
follow_ups: Not yet combined with EXP-077's scale (80 leaves): this exploration uses 6-7 leaves, enough to prove both mechanisms, not enough to also re-measure generative fidelity degradation -- a combined run (EXP-077's scale, with cross-page consistency checking turned on) is a natural next step.

extract_fact_triple's prepositional-object fallback (this exploration's prerequisite fix) still misses some constructions -- a compound date ('5 January 2024') extracted as just '5' in one spot-check -- worth a dedicated pass if dates become a consistency-check target, not just addresses/employers.
Not yet wired into lab.common.brain.reason as a signal -- this module is callable standalone, not yet reachable through the same entry point every other capability in this repo goes through.
models_used: flan-t5-small via lab.common.rewriter_backends (rewriter role only, fidelity-gated, falling back to deterministic text per leaf on any failure, exactly as EXP-048 measured) -- the pipeline is model-agnostic (EXP-076) and works with any registered checkpoint.
